Seminar Title:

Passive Acoustic Detection and Classification of Underwater Targets using Hybrid Signal Processing and Machine Learning Strategies

Seminar Type:

Jonnalagadda Srinivas

Abstract:

Underwater passive acoustic signals provide valuable information for the detection and classification of submerged and surface targets. Still, their analysis is challenging due to the nonlinear, nonstationary nature of acoustic signatures, background noise, signal distortion, and variations in target operating conditions. The present seminar focuses on developing a framework that integrates numerical acoustic modelling with advanced signal decomposition, denoising, time-frequency analysis, feature extraction and classification techniques for detecting and classifying the underwater acoustic targets. As an initial stage of the research, controlled synthetic acoustic signals representing multicomponent sinusoidal, exponentially decaying frequency-modulated, and amplitude-modulated signal characteristics are generated under different additive white Gaussian noise conditions. A multi-stage signal-processing approach was implemented in which wavelet-based denoising is followed by empirical mode decomposition. The resulting intrinsic mode functions are further analyzed using the Hilbert-Huang Transforms to characterize the non-stationary and instantaneous-frequency behavior of the signals. Statistical amplitude-domain and instantaneous-frequency-domain features are subsequently extracted for target classification. A preliminary classification framework based on a general regression neural network was implemented and evaluated using controlled synthetic data at different signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) levels. The initial results demonstrate the potential of the proposed combination of denoising, signal decomposition, and feature extraction techniques to discriminate among different signal classes. The preliminary study achieved an overall classification accuracy of 98.67% on the controlled synthetic dataset, providing an initial validation of the proposed processing strategy. The future work plan will be also presented.
